clue.text: Outline beginnings of chapters in rough with writer

indicators.note: beginnings of asks for the opening letter of each of the three following words

parts.note: cum is Latin for with, as in 'bed-cum-sitting room'
a scribe is one who writes, a copyist or author

explanation.surface: An author drafts a rough summary of the opening chapters of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginnings of' takes C, I and R from 'chapters in rough'; 'in rough' reads as a phrase meaning in draft, which hides that 'in' gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To circumscribe is to draw a line round something, so to outline or bound it.

clue.text: Garment worn by female Conservative at clubs, perhaps

parts.note: clubs are one of the four suits in a pack of cards, so 'perhaps' marks an example

explanation.surface: A woman Tory politician turns up at nightclubs in a striking outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like nightclubs; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A catsuit is a close-fitting one-piece outfit covering body and legs, chiefly worn by women.

clue.text: Charge aimlessly with expedition

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'
idly means without purpose, aimlessly

explanation.surface: Someone rushes about without purpose on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' suggests a journey; here it means speed, as in 'expeditious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed, so doing something with expedition is doing it quickly.

clue.text: Having canvas hung up in special laundries

indicators.note: special is read as unusual or specially prepared, telling us to rework the word laundries

explanation.surface: Canvas is hung up to dry in purpose-built washhouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas hung up' looks like washing on a line; canvas is sail, hoisted aloft on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship under sail has its sails set and is moving by wind power, that is with its canvas raised.

clue.text: Second president's murderer

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower; with the possessive it gives IKES

explanation.surface: A news line about a later president's assassin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second president' looks like John Adams; it is two pieces, S and Ike's.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Sikes is the brutal killer of Nancy in Dickens's novel Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Criminal schemes that'll bring opponents to court

definitions.meaning: dishonest money-making operations such as extortion
the bats used in tennis and similar games played on a court; a court game in its own right

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fraudulent enterprises and the strung bats of court games like tennis.

clue.text: American's mistake identifying British caterpillar

parts.note: a looper is a caterpillar of the geometer moth, which moves by arching its body into a loop

explanation.surface: A US visitor wrongly names an insect larva found in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooper is American slang for an embarrassing error or gaffe.

clue.text: One claims it's a free country

parts.note: things made one are united
to state is to claim or assert, so claims gives states

explanation.surface: A patriot asserts that their homeland is free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One claims' reads as a person making a claim; it is two pieces, UNITED and STATES.
explanation.definitionFit: America calls itself the land of the free, so it is a nation fairly called a free country.

clue.text: It may contain brief accounts of old man in famous case

indicators.note: in says the father goes inside the word for famous
case says the word for famous forms the outer shell holding the other piece

parts.note: noted means well known, famous
old man is informal for father, giving pa

explanation.surface: A celebrated legal case file holds a short record of an old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'famous case' looks like a celebrated trial; 'case' is the container signal around NOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper for jottings holds short written records such as memos.

clue.text: Dismiss i.e. remove from field of play

definitions.meaning: to dismiss someone is to throw them out of a job or place
in football the ball is kicked out of play, over the touchline

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to eject someone and to boot the ball off the pitch.

clue.text: Greek food featured regularly in articles? Just the opposite

definitions.text: Greek food featured regularly in articles? Just the opposite

parts.words: Greek food featured regularly in articles? Just the opposite
parts.note: the indefinite article appears at every other position in the name of the dish, so the articles feature regularly in the food rather than the food in articles

explanation.surface: A Greek dish crops up often in magazine features.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests food writing; in fact every second letter of the answer is A, the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Taramasalata is a Greek dip made from fish roe, bread or potato, oil and lemon.

clue.text: Speak strongly in protest and get a clap?

definitions.meaning: to rage or roar against something, as a preacher does from a pulpit
a clap of noise in a storm, so the question mark marks the playful sense

explanation.definitionFit: To thunder is to denounce loudly, and a thunderclap is the storm's sudden crash.

clue.text: Cleaning device for back

definitions.meaning: a carpet ... is a hand-pushed machine for cleaning floors
in football a back is a defender, and the ... is the free defender behind the main back line

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a floor-cleaning machine and a defensive football position.

clue.text: Extremely dicey to include outrageous eccentric

indicators.note: to include says the outer letters wrap round the other piece
extremely points to the extremities, the first and last letters of dicey

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means outrageous or excessive

explanation.surface: Someone eccentric is willing to take wild, risky chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'dicey'; it takes D and Y, which go round OTT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty is informal for mildly mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Ruminates about what might prevent disease

indicators.note: about here means round about, in a jumbled order, so the letters of ruminates are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker muses on how illness could be avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiserum is a blood serum containing antibodies, given to protect against a particular infection.

clue.text: Rude word, perhaps? It's about time girl got up

indicators.note: about says the turned girl's name goes around the other piece
in a down clue, got up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Margaret is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark that a girl was finally out of bed, prompting a swear word.
explanation.walkthrough: A tetragram is a four-letter word, the classic euphemism for a swear word, hence 'perhaps?'. Read upwards, 'got up' turns MARGARET into TERAGRAM, which goes 'about' T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word of four letters, and many coarse words famously have four.

clue.text: He gets new types off to a flying start

definitions.text: He gets new types off to a flying start

parts.words: He gets new types off to a flying start
parts.note: one whose job is to take newly built kinds of aircraft into the air for the first time

explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies prototype aircraft, so new models literally make their first flights with him.

clue.text: Disliked person also interrupting moderate

indicators.note: interrupting says one word breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: so-so means middling, moderate
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: An unpopular man keeps cutting in on the chairman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moderate' looks like a verb, to chair a debate; it is the adjective, SO-SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a so-and-so is a euphemism for an unpleasant or disliked person.

clue.text: Occupied as new Pope provided guidance

indicators.note: new means the letters of pope are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: led means guided, showed the way

explanation.surface: A newly elected pontiff took up residence and directed the faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' in the surface is the pontiff; here 'new' tells us to rearrange its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A land that is peopled has inhabitants, that is, it is populated or occupied.

clue.text: One who filled diary with encoded pages? Yes

indicators.note: encoded means put into code, scrambled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone kept a journal written in cipher and confirms it.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys famously wrote his diary in shorthand, so 'encoded' fits the surface as well as signalling the anagram of PP and YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept a celebrated diary of 1660s London, including the Great Fire.

clue.text: Not supporting any international group in this part of speech

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
no means not any, as in 'no help'
UN is the United Nations

explanation.surface: A statement of neutrality: backing no global organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not supporting any' is rephrased as 'supporting no', PRO + NO; 'this' signals that the clue's own word 'this' is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as 'this', 'he' and 'it' stand in for nouns and form their own class of speech.

clue.text: Election of chief

definitions.meaning: in the US a preliminary vote choosing a party's candidate
main or principal, as in 'of chief importance'

explanation.definitionFit: Primary means both a nominating vote and first in importance.

clue.text: New toga exchanged for another garment

indicators.note: exchanged means the letters of new toga swap places into a new order

explanation.surface: A toga is swapped for a different outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like a description of the toga; it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea gown is a loose, light dress once worn by women for afternoon tea at home.

clue.text: Without any chance of success currently at home

parts.note: now means at present, currently
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A hopeless situation for someone sitting at home right now.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where every outcome is bad, so success is impossible.

clue.text: Unfriendly and also agitated about spies

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the other piece
agitated means stirred up, shaken, so the letters of also are rearranged

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, a body of spies

explanation.surface: Someone cold and nervous about being watched by secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns ALSO into ASOL, which goes 'about' CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding the company of others, not sociable.

clue.text: As a rule, everything it predicts is wrong

definitions.text: As a rule, everything it predicts is wrong

parts.words: As a rule, everything it predicts is wrong
parts.note: a rule, in the sense of a supposed law, which forecasts that whatever can go wrong will go wrong

explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' reads as 'usually'; here it means the answer is itself a rule. Sod's Law is the British name for Murphy's Law.
explanation.definitionFit: Sod's Law is the British name for the jokey principle that if something can go wrong, it will.

clue.text: One way to calm disturbances in port — with diplomacy

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port, often shortened to Rio
tact is skill in handling people, diplomacy

explanation.surface: Authorities hope to settle unrest in a harbour city by careful negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading the Riot Act, a British law of 1714, ordered rioters to disperse; the phrase now means a stern warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the Riot Act was a legal step that ordered crowds to disperse, to restore order.

clue.text: Notes collapsing individual under my protection

parts.note: folding means collapsing, as a folding chair does

indicators.note: under says the single person is placed beneath the cover of the other word
protection says the word my shelters the other piece inside it

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Banknotes given as a folding individual is kept safe under someone's wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like a verb or jottings; it means banknotes, which fold, unlike coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding money is slang for paper currency, as opposed to coins.
